strategies.name: fvg_trend_continuation_entry
element_inventory: FVG detection: a fair value gap / imbalance is where price moved so aggressively in one direction that it left a gap between candles without proper trading activity
FVG is created across three candlesticks; map the gap from the closing point of the FIRST candle to the opening point of the THIRD candle — the space in between is the imbalance
Bullish FVG (buy setup): gap mapped from first-candle close to third-candle open on an up-move
Bearish FVG (sell setup): gap mapped from first-candle close to third-candle open on a down-move
PRECONDITION — trade only in the direction of the prevailing trend/momentum (this is a trend-continuation entry; only take FVG entries aligned with the trend)
PRECONDITION / filter — the imbalance must have caused a break of structure; only consider the FVG that created the break of structure (look at the three candlesticks before that break of structure)
SELECTION rule — do not map out every FVG on the chart; select only the FVG that caused the break of structure
PRECONDITION / filter — there must be liquidity that price clears before tapping into the imbalance
SELECTION rule — prefer the FVG that is very close to the order block (price tends to target the FVG nearest the order block and react from it)
ENTRY — wait for price to retrace and tap into the selected FVG, then enter in the trend-continuation direction (price taps in and continues pushing)
STOP (buy) — place stop loss a little bit below the FVG
STOP (sell) — place stop loss a little bit above the FVG
STOP constraint — do not drag the stop loss to also accommodate the order block; keep the stop just beyond the FVG only (dragging it to cover the order block kills the risk-to-reward)
